correctness.rationale: Projection of any product return chain cannot increase an error coordinate, proving the lower bound. For p=infinity, concatenate factor return chains to a common length; the maximum step error is unchanged, giving equality. In the finite systems, any return of cost below the large distance D must follow the deterministic chain and use only the unique unit reset, so factor return lengths are multiples of L or M with one unit reset per block. A product return length must be a common multiple. On one lcm block, the union of reset times has M/g+L/g-1 elements because only the terminal reset is simultaneous, so the l^p cost is exactly the claimed root. Repeating a block increases finite-p cost and any D-jump is more expensive by construction. This is an exact all-parameter proof; no missing verifier artifact is treated as evidence.
